description: The bar chart illustrates the performance comparison of three quality metrics — IFD, Quality Scores, and DEITA — under two different averaging schemes: object-level (Avg_obj) and subject-level (Avg_sub), as evaluated in the context of the MIG method for automatic data selection in instruction tuning. The vertical axis represents “Scores,” ranging from 30 to 70 in increments of 5, while the horizontal axis lists the three quality metrics. For each metric, two bars are shown: a light blue bar for Avg_obj and a light orange bar for Avg_sub, with their exact numerical values labeled above each bar. Additionally, two horizontal dashed lines indicate baseline averages: a blue dashed line at 63.98 for Base Avg_obj and an orange dashed line at 37.91 for Base Avg_sub. The Avg_obj scores are 63.98 (IFD), 66.06 (Quality Scores), and 67.64 (DEITA), all exceeding the Base Avg_obj baseline. The Avg_sub scores are 41.90 (IFD), 39.13 (Quality Scores), and 42.99 (DEITA), all above the Base Avg_sub baseline of 37.91. The chart visually emphasizes that DEITA achieves the highest Avg_obj score (67.64), while IFD achieves the highest Avg_sub score (42.99), suggesting DEITA performs best under object-level averaging and IFD under subject-level averaging relative to their respective baselines.
